```{r packages, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(spax)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

spax ships open data for general practice (GP) care in NHS Cornwall and Isles
of Scilly, in south-west England. The guides use them, so this page
introduces each object once: what it holds, how the objects fit together and
what they cannot tell you. Nothing needs downloading.

| Object | What it holds | How to load it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `cornwall_gp` | 55 GP practices: location, GP workforce and list size | Loaded with spax |
| `cornwall_lsoa` | 337 small areas: boundaries, population and registered residents | Loaded with spax |
| `cornwall_flows` | Registered residents by small area and practice | Loaded with spax |
| `cornwall_travel` | Travel minutes from each small area to each practice | Loaded with spax |
| `cornwall_pop.tif` | Population grid, about 1 km cells | `read_spax_example()` |
| `cornwall_gp_travel.tif` | Travel minutes from each grid cell to each practice | `read_spax_example()` |

Each object has a help page with every column, for example `?cornwall_gp`.

## Practices

`cornwall_gp` is an `sf` point layer in British National Grid coordinates
(EPSG:27700), one row per practice. `practice` is the NHS practice code, which
links the practices to the flows and to the travel times.

```{r practices}
gp <- st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
gp |>
  select(practice, name, gp_fte_extg, gp_fte, list_size) |>
  head()
```

The guides use `gp_fte_extg` as supply: full-time equivalent GPs (37.5 hours a
week) excluding GPs in training, from the June 2026 workforce data. GPs in
training are left out because their recording changed in June 2018 and they
cluster in training practices; `gp_fte` includes them. `list_size` counts all
patients registered at the practice. Each practice is placed at its main site;
branch surgeries are not represented.

## Small areas

`cornwall_lsoa` holds the 337 Lower layer Super Output Areas (LSOA 2021), small
areas of about 1,000 to 3,400 residents. Each has an ONS mid-2024
population estimate (`pop`, also by age band) and the number of its residents
registered at any GP practice in England (`registered`). That number splits
into residents registered at a practice in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
(`registered_in`) and those registered elsewhere (`registered_out`).

```{r small-areas}
areas <- st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)

# Registered residents split into inside and outside the area's practices
stopifnot(all(areas$registered == areas$registered_in + areas$registered_out))

c(
  small_areas = nrow(areas),
  population = sum(areas$pop),
  registered = sum(areas$registered),
  registered_outside = sum(areas$registered_out)
)

# Rural-urban classification (2021), in three broad groups
table(sub(":.*", "", areas$ruc21))
```

Registered counts exceed the population estimates by about 4%, reflecting
list inflation and the different reference dates. The map shows the small
areas by broad rural-urban class, with the practices on top.

```{r areas-map, fig.alt = "Map of the 337 small areas of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly coloured by broad rural-urban class (urban, larger rural, smaller rural), with the 55 GP practices as black points."}
# Small areas with a broad rural-urban class
classed <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  mutate(class = sub(":.*", "", ruc21))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = classed,
    aes(fill = class),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = cornwall_gp, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Rural-urban class",
    values = c(
      Urban = "#5b7fa6",
      `Larger rural` = "#a9c48f",
      `Smaller rural` = "#e3dca8"
    )
  ) +
  labs(title = "Small areas (LSOA 2021) and GP practices") +
  theme_void()
```

The Isles of Scilly are the small group of islands off the western tip.

## Registrations

`cornwall_flows` counts the residents of each small area registered at each of
the 55 practices, one row per pair that has at least one registration.

```{r flows}
head(cornwall_flows)

# Row totals of the flows are the residents registered in the area
by_area <- tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$lsoa, sum)
stopifnot(all(by_area[areas$lsoa] == areas$registered_in))

c(
  pairs = nrow(cornwall_flows),
  registered_residents = sum(cornwall_flows$patients)
)
```

A registration is a **stock**: who is registered with which practice at one
date (July 2026). It is not a count of visits and says nothing about how often
people use their practice. Residents counted in `registered_out` are
registered with a practice outside Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, for
example in Devon; they are not people without a practice. The allocation
guides fit a model to these registrations; the FCA guides do not use them.

## Travel times

`cornwall_travel` is a matrix of motorised travel minutes from each small
area's population-weighted centroid (rows, `cornwall_lsoa$lsoa`) to each
practice's main site (columns, `cornwall_gp$practice`).

```{r travel}
cornwall_travel[1:3, 1:4]

# Minutes from each small area to its nearest practice
nearest <- apply(cornwall_travel, 1, min, na.rm = TRUE)
summary(nearest)
```

The times are least-cost paths through a 2019 global friction surface with
cells of about 1 km. They are rounded to whole minutes with a floor of one
minute, so at least half of the small areas have a nearest practice at 1
minute. Traffic is not modelled, and in towns several practices can share one
cell.

```{r nearest-map, fig.alt = "Map of the small areas of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly coloured by travel minutes to the nearest GP practice, from 1 to 13 minutes; the longest times are inland in the east and at the western tip."}
# Join each area's nearest-practice time to its polygon
nearest_map <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  mutate(minutes = nearest[lsoa])

ggplot(nearest_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = minutes), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Minutes", option = "magma", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = "Travel time to the nearest GP practice") +
  theme_void()
```

## The grids

Two GeoTIFF files cover the same 30 arc-second grid (about 1 km, in
longitude and latitude). `cornwall_pop.tif` holds WorldPop 2020 estimated
residents per cell: a **count**, not a density. `cornwall_gp_travel.tif` holds
one layer of travel minutes per practice, named by practice code.
`read_spax_example()` reads both.

```{r grids}
pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")

c(
  cells = ncell(pop),
  populated_cells = sum(!is.na(values(pop))),
  travel_layers = nlyr(travel_grid),
  grid_residents = round(global(pop, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]),
  ons_residents = sum(areas$pop)
)
```

```{r pop-map, fig.alt = "Raster map of the WorldPop 2020 population grid for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly in residents per cell, in six classes; most cells hold fewer than 50 residents and the towns stand out with several hundred or more."}
plot(
  pop,
  breaks = c(0, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 5000),
  col = hcl.colors(6, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE),
  axes = FALSE,
  main = "WorldPop 2020: residents per cell (about 1 km)",
  plg = list(title = "Residents")
)
```

The grid total is about 7% below the ONS mid-2024 estimate used in
`cornwall_lsoa`. The two are different sources and dates; choose one for an
analysis and say which. The FCA guides use the grid; the allocation guides use
registered residents of the small areas.

In the travel grid, `NA` marks unpopulated cells, pairs with no road
connection and journeys over 180 minutes.

## The Isles of Scilly and the mainland

The Isles of Scilly have one small area and one practice, St Mary's Health
Centre (`L82017`). The road-based travel times cannot cross the sea, so the
islands and the mainland cannot reach each other: their travel times are `NA`.

```{r scilly}
# Unknown travel times in the small-area matrix: the Scilly area's row and
# the Scilly practice's column
c(
  unknown = sum(is.na(cornwall_travel)),
  scilly_area = sum(is.na(cornwall_travel[areas$scilly, ])),
  scilly_practice = sum(is.na(cornwall_travel[, gp$scilly]))
)
```

The islands do have access to the mainland, by boat and air, which these
travel times do not represent. Rather than treat the islands as cut off, the
guides model **mainland Cornwall only**: 336 small areas and 54 practices,
selected with the `scilly` column.

```{r mainland}
mainland_areas <- filter(areas, !scilly)
mainland_gp <- filter(gp, !scilly)
c(small_areas = nrow(mainland_areas), practices = nrow(mainland_gp))
```

In the allocation guides, mainland residents registered with the Scilly
practice or outside Cornwall therefore count as registered outside mainland
Cornwall. [Preparing your own data](data-prep.html) shows what the unknown
travel times do to an FCA index if the islands are kept.

## Sources, dates and licences

| Data | Objects | Source and date | Licence |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Registrations | `cornwall_gp`, `cornwall_lsoa`, `cornwall_flows` | NHS England, Patients Registered at a GP Practice, July 2026 | Open Government Licence v3.0 |
| GP workforce | `cornwall_gp` | NHS England, General Practice Workforce, 30 June 2026 | Open Government Licence v3.0 |
| Practice locations | `cornwall_gp` | ONS Postcode Directory, November 2025 | Open Government Licence v3.0; contains OS and Royal Mail data |
| Boundaries, centroids, population | `cornwall_lsoa` | ONS LSOA 2021 boundaries and rural-urban classification, population-weighted centroids, mid-2024 population estimates | Open Government Licence v3.0; contains OS data |
| Population grid | `cornwall_pop.tif` | WorldPop, 2020 UN-adjusted 1 km estimates | Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 |
| Travel times | `cornwall_travel`, `cornwall_gp_travel.tif` | Derived by the package author from the Malaria Atlas Project 2019 motorised friction surface (Weiss et al. 2020) | Creative Commons Attribution; version not yet confirmed |

The package's MIT licence does not cover these data. Keep the dates in mind
when reading results: the registrations and the workforce are from 2026, the
population grid from 2020, the small-area population from mid-2024 and the
road network from about 2019. The full attributions, with the required
wording for each source, are installed with the package:

```{r copyrights, eval = FALSE}
file.show(system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax"))
```
